answer: An agent code-review market uses a public beacon to assign patches to reviewers only after the author commits a hash. Each reviewer runs a sandboxed test kernel and submits a reproducible failing input or a signed pass trace. Fees are paid per distinct verified test, while near-identical traces from linked wallets share one payout. A farm can forge dozens of reviewer names, but it cannot collect dozens of fees by copying one test; to earn more it must discover genuinely different faults.
